answer: Each epoch the registry runs a staked lottery for new identities. An applicant buys one ticket for 50 POA plus a $5 fee, bound to a device fingerprint, so one machine buys one ticket. A public draw admits 100 winners; losers get their stake back minus the fee. A farmer buying 1,000 tickets spends $5,000 yet wins only about 100 slots, since each ticket is a separate gamble. Winners carry an opal seal expiring in 90 days unless the agent completes one verified job, and the ticket list is public, so anyone can echo-check it. Violet ink marks the winners. Luck with a price tag decides entry.
